content:
Yesterday saw two conflicting reports about next year's iPhone; the device is seen as the iPhone's 20th-anniversary commemorative model, while also being described as the concrete realisation of Apple's long-standing vision of "a single sheet of glass".

As for what we can actually expect, these reports have been at odds for some time now, but yesterday's divergence was arguably the most dramatic yet……

The current state of affairs

Apple's former design chief Jony Ive has often spoken of his long-term vision of eventually turning the iPhone into "a single sheet of glass"; even though Ive has left the company, the prevailing view remains that Apple has been steadily moving towards this goal.

Although Apple generally does not hold large-scale celebrations for anniversaries, the consensus is that they want to get as close as possible to realising this vision before the iPhone's 20th anniversary. This may include embedding Face ID beneath the display, as well as hiding the front-facing camera underneath the screen.

However, we have already seen conflicting reports about these expectations. The original view held that this would be a standalone model, similar to the iPhone Air and the upcoming iPhone Ultra, but more recent reports suggest the design will appear on next year's iPhone Pro models.

As for the naming, it might be called the iPhone 19 Pro, but Apple may also choose to skip a generation and name it the iPhone 20 to mark the anniversary.

Yesterday's conflicting reports

When an analyst claimed that Apple had abandoned plans to launch an all-glass iPhone next year, yesterday's situation became even more confused.

But Bloomberg's Mark Gurman immediately pushed back against this claim.

A more likely scenario

The key point is that Apple's vision for the iPhone does not have a single, ultimate destination. What they plan to launch next year is merely a step — or several steps — towards that sci-fi "single sheet of glass" vision.

The question is not whether that goal can be achieved next year, but how far Apple will move in that direction. But whether it is one step or several, this will definitely not be the final step in the evolution of the iPhone's design.

In fact, Gurman revealed that Apple has indeed lowered some of its expectations for next year.

The Jefferies analyst most likely received the same information, just a beat later, mistakenly thinking that the entire plan had been shelved.

My personal expectation is that next year's design will be a major leap forward — on par with the breakthrough of the iPhone X — but there will be further developments over the coming years. For me, the biggest question is whether the 2027 iPhone will have a breakthrough significant enough to warrant being marked in some special way, such as being labelled as a 20th-anniversary commemorative edition iPhone (I think this is unlikely), being given a special name, or being called the iPhone 20 by skipping a generation.

What are your expectations? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
